name: r2-external-1
statement: On Olmo-3 the RL-Zero-Math delta moves the output about 700 times more per unit of weight energy than a random direction does, because its signs are coherent, so DARE's rescaling noise costs at most about the delta's own KL down to q = 0.1 % and the plateau must end in a sharp cliff near q = 0.01 %; within that range the noise acts on generation as a small fixed random logit distortion that raises the surprise of generated text and so weakens self-reinforcing repetition: random-sign weight noise reduces loops and adds accuracy on a looping model at T 0.6 and costs a little at T 1.0, where there are no loops to break.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base, Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math, partial and noisy copies of the MLP delta (DARE, random-sign sparse noise), MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 and T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, plain and cued prompts. Also covers DARE failing on SFT deltas (bytegraft, Think-SFT) through their low sign coherence. Does not cover the residual 10.6-point cued-base gap at T 1.0, the 'Answer:' format change, or which neurons carry the signal.

explains.how: With leverage L ~ 700, DARE noise KL is (1-q)/(q L) of the MLP delta's KL: 0.05x at q = 3 %, 0.14x at 1 %, 1.4x at 0.1 %, all small enough that accuracy is flat across q.

explains.quote: DARE's realized change energy is 33 to 1,000 times the whole delta's
explains.how: Energy is the wrong yardstick: the extra energy points in random directions, which carry about 1/700 of the KL per unit energy of the sign-coherent RL delta.
The same leverage ratio predicts DARE equals the whole MLP delta down to q ~ 0.1 %, and not below it.
An SFT delta has leverage near 5, so a 1 % or 0.1 % DARE copy adds noise with 20-200x the delta's own KL, and the model collapses.

explains.quote: the imitation delta (24.8% of norm, 100x larger)
explains.how: A large, imitation-trained delta is the low-leverage case; the theory predicts DARE fails on Think-SFT as it did on bytegraft.
The RL delta is small enough that its effect and the noise's effect stay in the quadratic (Fisher) regime that the leverage estimate assumes.
Linear additivity of neuron contributions confirms the small-perturbation regime in which KL scales with energy times leverage.
A random weight edit of matched norm lowered the repeated-10-gram share on a looping model: random weight noise weakens repetition.

explains.quote: one random column set matched on weight norm 28/300 (9.3 %)
explains.how: On a cap-limited, looping model the random edit doubled accuracy over the base's 14/300, the loop-breaking dividend this theory assigns to random-direction noise.
On the cued base at T 0.6, any source of extra surprise in the generated text (here the restored tail) cuts loops and raises accuracy.

explains.quote: on the longest, cap hits fall 32.8 points and accuracy holds
explains.how: More randomness helps where loops dominate and hurts where they do not (short problems lose 28 points), the two-sided effect that makes the sign of the noise effect flip between T 0.6 and T 1.0.

explains.quote: Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats
explains.how: Sets the scale: DARE 0.1 % noise should add about 0.1 nats per token, the KL of a temperature change of roughly 0.1-0.2, while q = 0.01 % adds about 1 nat per token.

conflicts.quote: T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, plain prompt in chat template
conflicts.how: The plain base loops at this setting, yet DARE 0.1 % (largest noise) is not better than DARE 3 %; the theory must assume the DARE arms already took RL's loop resistance from the signal, so the noise has few loops left to break.
The random edit cut cap hits by only 5 points on Qwen3.5-0.8B with a presence penalty, a small effect on another model family.

conflicts.quote: Loop penalties: DRY costs 14.2 points on MATH-500
conflicts.how: A direct anti-repetition intervention lowered accuracy on Qwen3-4B, so weakening repetition does not always pay.

conflicts.quote: an off-target term absent in gemma and Qwen
conflicts.how: Edits in OLMo models spread through other positions more than in other families, which may make random noise in Olmo more damaging per unit energy than the leverage estimate assumes.

rival: The standing accounts (r1-all-2 saturating switch, r1-surprises-2 low-rank function with inert high-rank noise) say the noise is simply inert: it neither helps nor hurts at any q. Separation: (1) random-sign sparse noise with DARE 0.1 %'s energy and zero expected value, added to the cued base at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95: the rivals predict 354 +- 15 right and ~119 cap hits; this theory predicts ~85 cap hits and ~378 right. (2) DARE at q = 0.01 %: the rivals predict the plateau holds (~85 %); this theory predicts collapse below 200/500.

predictions.experiment: Teacher-forced on the 80 stored MATH-500 answers of result-156f7b, all positions after the cue: mean KL(edited || base) per token for base + random-sign sparse noise on the MLP (each MLP delta entry kept with probability 0.001, multiplied by 1,000 and by an independent random sign, zero expected value), divided by mean KL(RL || base) on the same positions
predictions.refuted_by: ratio above 10 (random-direction noise is not ~700x less effective than the RL delta in Olmo) or below 0.1

predictions.experiment: Base + the same random-sign sparse MLP noise (one draw), opening cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample: cap hits (base + cue at this setting: 119)
predictions.refuted_by: 112 or more cap hits (the noise does not weaken loops)

predictions.experiment: Same run as above: right (base + cue at this setting: 354)
Base + the same random-sign sparse MLP noise (same draw), opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample: right (base + cue at this setting: 410)
predictions.refuted_by: 412 or more right (noise helps without loops, so its effect is not loop-breaking) or below 360 (the noise is not small)

predictions.experiment: DARE on the MLP delta at q = 0.01 % (each MLP delta entry kept with probability 0.0001, scaled by 10,000), rest base, plain prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, MATH-500 n=500, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample
predictions.refuted_by: 380 or more right (the DARE plateau continues past the leverage limit)

imports.finding: For Olmo-3-7B RL-Zero deltas the Fisher curvature along the RL direction is ~708x that of a random same-norm direction, the effect sits in sign coherence, and DARE damage follows (1-p)/(p*rho_sign).
imports.how: Converts the team's 'DARE carries 33-1,000x the energy' into a KL budget: the noise costs 0.05-1.4x the delta's own KL across q = 3 %-0.1 %, which is why the curve is flat, and it predicts a cliff at q = 0.01 % that the team's items do not imply (n13 even suggests a wide plateau).

imports.finding: Repetition rate is a near-linear function of the cross-entropy of generated text: low surprise leads to the boredom trap (repetition), high surprise to the confusion trap (incoherence).
imports.how: Turns the random-direction KL into a sign-flipping effect on accuracy: the same noise lowers loops and helps the cued base at T 0.6 (boredom side) and costs it at T 1.0 (confusion side), a prediction about a random weight edit that neither paper nor any team item makes.

imports.finding: Sentence-level repetition self-reinforces, and text with higher initial probability reinforces faster.
imports.how: Explains why a small fixed logit distortion matters for loops at all: lowering the probability of the repeated block at the first repeats keeps the self-reinforcing loop from locking in, so a small KL has a large effect on cap hits.
